Online Income Tax Calculator: Old vs. New Tax Regime (FY 2025-26)

Navigating the nuances of Indian income tax computations can often feel overwhelming, particularly when deciding which tax structure suits your financial situation. The Online Income Tax Calculator (FY 2025-26 / AY 2026-27) is built to instantly compute your estimated tax liability, compare your outcomes across both tax regimes, and clarify how your salary breakdown, allowances, and investments impact your final tax payable.

How to Use the Indian Income Tax Calculator

To get the most accurate estimate from the calculator, gather your financial documents and follow these steps:

  1. Select Your Financial Year: Ensure the calculator is set to FY 2025-26 (Assessment Year 2026-27) to apply the correct active slab rates.

  2. Enter Gross Income Details: Input your salary components, including basic salary, dearness allowance, special allowances, and any income from other sources (such as interest or rental income).

  3. Input Allowances & Deductions (Old Regime): If you are evaluating the old tax regime, enter your actual rent paid for HRA calculations, life insurance premiums, PPF investments under Section 80C, health insurance under Section 80D, and home loan interest.

  4. Run the Comparison: Click calculate to view a side-by-side output showing your taxable income and net tax liability under both the Old and New Tax Regimes.

Calculator Methodology & Formula Logic

Understanding the underlying computational steps ensures you can audit your figures and verify how the tool derives your final tax payable.

Step 1: Gross Total Income & Allowances

The calculation begins by aggregating all streams of income into your Gross Total Income (GTI). From this aggregate figure, standard deductions (such as the standard salary deduction) and permissible exemptions like House Rent Allowance (HRA) or Leave Travel Allowance (LTA) under the old regime are subtracted to arrive at your net figure before Chapter VI-A deductions.

Step 2: Deductions & Exemptions (Old Regime)

Under the Old Tax Regime, eligible deductions such as investments under Section 80C (capped at ₹1,50,000), medical insurance under Section 80D, and interest paid on housing loans under Section 24 are subtracted from your taxable base. Under the New Tax Regime, these specific deductions are omitted in exchange for lower baseline tax rates.

Step 3: Tax Slab Computation & Rebates (Section 87A)

Once net taxable income is determined, applicable slab rates are applied. After computing the tentative tax, the tool factors in the tax rebate under Section 87A and any applicable marginal relief, followed by the addition of health and education cess (4%).

Income Tax Slabs & Rates for FY 2025-26 (AY 2026-27)

Tax liability varies significantly depending on the regime you select. The tables below outline the active slabs for the current financial year.

(Note: Senior citizens and super senior citizens enjoy higher basic exemption thresholds of ₹3,00,000 and ₹5,00,000 respectively under the old regime).

Key Differences: Old Tax Regime vs. New Tax Regime

Choosing the right structure requires balancing deductions against tax rates:

  • Deductions: The Old Regime permits over 70 tax exemptions and deductions (including 80C, 80D, HRA, and LTA). The New Regime removes almost all deductions, though the standard deduction applies to salaried individuals under both structures.

  • Tax Slabs: The New Regime features wider tax slabs and lower baseline rates at various income tiers, making it beneficial for individuals with minimal traditional investments.

  • Flexibility: Salaried individuals can generally switch between regimes annually when filing their Income Tax Returns (ITR), whereas business owners face stricter limitations on switching.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

  • 1. Which tax regime should I choose using the calculator?

    If your total deductions (HRA, 80C, 80D, home loan interest) exceed the threshold where the lower tax rates of the New Regime become more advantageous, the Old Regime usually results in lower tax payable. Use the calculator to test your exact figures.

  • 2. Is the Standard Deduction available in both tax regimes?

    Yes, the standard deduction is available to salaried individuals and pensioners under both the Old and New Tax Regimes for FY 2025-26.

  • 3. What documents do I need before using the calculator?

    Keep your current salary slips, Form 16 (if available), rent receipts or agreements if claiming HRA, and investment proofs for Section 80C and 80D handy.

  • 4. How does the Section 87A rebate work?

    Section 87A provides a tax rebate that can eliminate tax liability entirely if your net taxable income falls below specified statutory limits under each regime.

  • 5. Can I switch my tax regime after submitting investment proofs to my employer?

    Yes. Even if you declare one regime to your employer for TDS deduction purposes, you have the legal right to choose the alternative regime when filing your personal ITR at the end of the financial year.

  • 6. Are maintenance charges included when calculating HRA exemptions?

    No. Only the core rent paid to the landlord is considered; separate utility bills and society maintenance fees are excluded.

  • 7. What happens if my income exceeds ₹50 lakhs?

    High-income earners are subject to a surcharge on their income tax liability. The calculator incorporates applicable surcharge tiers based on your gross income input.

  • 8. Does the calculator account for cess?

    Yes, the final computed tax output automatically adds the standard 4% Health and Education Cess mandated by the Income Tax Act.

  • 9. Is my financial data stored when I use this online tool?

    No calculations or financial figures input into the browser utility are retained on external servers, ensuring complete privacy.

  • 10. Can freelancers use this income tax calculator?

    While the tool accommodates standard salary breakdowns, freelancers and business owners should also account for professional expenses and presumptive taxation provisions under Section 44AD.

Important Legal & Verification Notices

This calculator and guide are provided for estimation, educational simulation, and tax planning purposes only. Tax laws are subject to amendment, and individual circumstances vary. Users are strongly advised to verify all computed tax liabilities and consult a qualified Chartered Accountant (CA) or review official CBDT portals prior to filing official Income Tax Returns (ITR).

faqs.question: Do I need to create an account to use an online tax calculator?
faqs.answer: No. Most quality online tax calculators allow you to run instant estimates anonymously without requiring registration or logins.

faqs.question: Are online tax calculations legally binding for filing?
faqs.answer: No. Calculators are estimation tools designed to help you plan. Your final tax liability is determined when you officially file your Income Tax Return (ITR) on the government portal.

faqs.question: Can freelancers and business owners use a standard tax calculator?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the calculator includes fields for business income, professional receipts, and allowable business expenses alongside regular salary inputs.

faqs.question: What happens if I make a mistake while entering my deductions?
faqs.answer: Since the calculator is an estimation tool, any input error simply alters the estimated output. You can re-enter the correct figures instantly to see the revised tax amount.

faqs.question: Is capital gains tax calculated automatically by online calculators?
faqs.answer: It depends on the platform. Advanced calculators provide specific input fields for short-term and long-term capital gains so they can apply the correct separate tax rates.

faqs.question: How often are online tax calculators updated with new budget rules?
faqs.answer: Reliable tax calculator platforms update their backend logic immediately following the Union Budget announcements and official notifications issued for the relevant financial year.

faqs.question: What is marginal relief, and how does it save me money if my income slightly exceeds ₹12 Lakhs?
faqs.answer: If your taxable income crosses ₹12 Lakhs under the New Tax Regime, your tax liability cannot exceed the amount of income earned above ₹12 Lakhs. Marginal relief absorbs the difference so you don't lose more money in tax than you did in extra earnings.

faqs.question: Is the 4% Health and Education Cess added automatically by tax calculators?
faqs.answer: Yes. Reliable online calculators compute your base tax across slabs, apply any eligible Section 87A rebates, and then add a final 4% Health and Education Cess to arrive at your net payable tax.

faqs.question: Can I claim an employer's NPS contribution under the New Tax Regime?
faqs.answer: Yes. Employer contributions to the National Pension System under Section 80CCD(2)—up to 14% of your basic salary—are deductible even if you choose the New Tax Regime.

faqs.question: What is the maximum surcharge difference between the Old and New Tax Regimes for high earners?
faqs.answer: For ultra-high-income earners with taxable income exceeding ₹5 Crores, the peak surcharge rate under the Old Tax Regime is 37%, whereas the New Tax Regime caps the maximum surcharge at 25%.

faqs.question: What happens if I miss the July 31st ITR filing deadline after calculating my tax?
faqs.answer: If you miss the standard July 31 deadline for non-audit cases, you can still file a belated return until December 31st of the assessment year, though it attracts late fees under Section 234F and potential interest penalties.

faqs.question: How does the ₹75,000 standard deduction make a salary of up to ₹12,75,000 tax-free under the New Regime?
faqs.answer: When your gross salary is ₹12,75,000, subtracting the ₹75,000 standard deduction brings your net taxable income down exactly to ₹12,00,000. The resulting tax liability is then entirely offset by the Section 87A rebate, resulting in zero net tax.

faqs.question: What happens if my salary changes mid-year? Should I recalculate quarterly?
faqs.answer: Yes. Receiving a mid-year appraisal, switching organizations, or earning unexpected bonuses alters your annual taxable income bracket. Running your figures through a dual-regime calculator quarterly ensures your monthly TDS aligns cleanly with your projected year-end liability.

faqs.question: Does the New Tax Regime affect my provident fund (EPF) or gratuity payouts?
faqs.answer: No. Statutory contributions to recognized Employee Provident Funds (EPF) and tax-exempt limits on gratuity or leave encashment are governed by separate statutory provisions and remain unaffected by your choice of tax regime.

faqs.question: Can I change my tax regime choice after submitting my employer declaration?
faqs.answer: Yes. Your declaration to your employer is only meant for calculating monthly TDS deductions. When filing your Income Tax Return (ITR) at the end of the year, you are completely free to choose whichever regime is more beneficial, provided you do not have business or professional income restrictions.

faqs.answer: If you are a business owner or professional opting out of the default New Tax Regime and you fail to file the required form within the stipulated statutory timeline, the tax authorities may default your filing to the New Tax Regime, potentially disrupting your anticipated tax liabilities.

faqs.answer: A taxpayer expecting their total tax liability to be lower than standard TDS rates can file Form 13 online on the TRACES portal under Section 197. The Assessing Officer issues a certificate specifying the lower deduction rate, which the deductor must apply upon verifying the certificate number.

faqs.question: Can I submit Form 15G or Form 15H to avoid TDS on interest income?
faqs.answer: Yes. If your estimated total taxable income for the financial year is below the basic exemption limit, you can submit Form 15G (for individuals under 60) or Form 15H (for senior citizens aged 60+) to the bank or deductor to prevent TDS deductions under Section 194A.

faqs.answer: Under Section 194C, TDS @ 1% (Individual/HUF) or 2% (Company/Firm) is deducted if a single invoice exceeds ₹30,000 or if the aggregate payments made to the contractor exceed ₹1,00,000 in a financial year.

faqs.question: How does Section 194Q on purchase of goods work?
faqs.answer: Buyers with gross business turnover exceeding ₹10 Crores in the preceding financial year must deduct TDS @ 0.1% on purchase of goods from a resident seller if total purchases exceed ₹50,00,000 in the current FY. TDS is computed strictly on the value exceeding ₹50 Lakhs.

faqs.question: When is TDS under Section 194S applicable on Crypto and Virtual Digital Assets?
faqs.answer: TDS @ 1% is deducted by the buyer or crypto exchange on consideration paid for the transfer of Virtual Digital Assets (cryptocurrency, tokens, NFTs) if the annual transaction value exceeds ₹10,000 (or ₹50,000 for specified individual buyers with no business income).

faqs.question: What is the due date for depositing TDS and filing quarterly returns?
faqs.answer: TDS deducted during any calendar month must be deposited to the government treasury by the 7th day of the subsequent month (April 30th for March). Quarterly returns (Form 24Q for salary, Form 26Q for non-salary) are due by July 31 (Q1), October 31 (Q2), January 31 (Q3), and May 31 (Q4).

faqs.question: How does the payee get credit for the TDS deducted?
faqs.answer: Once the deductor files the quarterly TDS return, the tax credit is mapped to the payee's PAN and reflected in their Annual Information Statement (AIS) and Form 26AS. The deductor also issues Form 16A (for non-salary) or Form 16 (for salary) generated from the TRACES portal.

posts.title: Pradhan Mantri Vidyalaxmi Scheme (PM-Vidyalaxmi): Eligibility, Education Loan, Interest Subsidy and How to Apply
posts.content:
Paying for higher education can become difficult even after a student gets admission to a good college. Tuition fees are only one part of the cost. Hostel charges, books, equipment, examination fees and other education expenses can push the total amount much higher.

The Pradhan Mantri Vidyalaxmi Scheme (PM-Vidyalaxmi) is designed to help eligible students access education loans for higher education in India. The scheme provides a special education-loan framework for students admitted to eligible Quality Higher Educational Institutions (QHEIs). It also provides interest-subvention support for eligible students from lower-income families.

The scheme was approved by the Union Cabinet on 6 November 2024. The official PM-Vidyalaxmi portal provides the online process for education-loan applications and interest-subvention claims.

Quick answer: PM-Vidyalaxmi is not a normal scholarship that simply deposits a fixed amount into every student's bank account. It primarily supports education loans for eligible students admitted to participating quality higher-education institutions. Eligible students can also receive interest-subvention support during the moratorium period, subject to the scheme's income and other conditions.

PM-Vidyalaxmi Scheme at a Glance

Particular

Details

Scheme

Pradhan Mantri Vidyalaxmi (PM-Vidyalaxmi)

Type

Central Sector Scheme

Main purpose

Education-loan support for higher education

Launch/approval

6 November 2024

Eligible institutions

Quality Higher Educational Institutions (QHEIs) identified under the scheme

Application portal

PM-Vidyalaxmi portal

Special loan feature

Collateral-free and guarantor-free education loan under the scheme

Interest support

3% interest subvention for eligible students with family income up to ₹8 lakh

Lower-income support

Full interest subvention during the moratorium for eligible students with family income up to ₹4.5 lakh

Credit guarantee

Government credit guarantee support for eligible loans up to ₹7.5 lakh

Application process

Online

Management quota

Education loans under management quota are not eligible under the scheme

The official PM-Vidyalaxmi FAQ confirms the income-based interest-subvention provisions, management-quota exclusion and credit-guarantee provision.

What is the PM-Vidyalaxmi Scheme?

PM-Vidyalaxmi is a Central Sector Scheme introduced by the Government of India to make education loans easier to access for students pursuing higher education in eligible institutions.

The key difference between PM-Vidyalaxmi and a conventional scholarship is simple: the main benefit is linked to an education loan.

A student first needs admission to an eligible institution and then applies for an education loan through the PM-Vidyalaxmi portal. The application is routed to the selected bank for processing.

The portal describes PM-Vidyalaxmi as a unified platform through which students can apply for education loans and interest-subvention benefits.

That distinction matters because a student should not assume that PM-Vidyalaxmi means the government will pay the entire college fee directly as a scholarship.

Who Can Benefit From PM-Vidyalaxmi?

The scheme is intended for students who secure merit-based admission to eligible Quality Higher Educational Institutions and need an education loan for their higher studies.

Your first check should therefore be the college or institution, not just your family income.

A student may have the required income level but still need to satisfy the other conditions of the scheme, including admission to an eligible institution and compliance with the applicable loan and scheme requirements.

The official PM-Vidyalaxmi portal maintains the list of institutions eligible under the scheme.

Why the college matters

Suppose you receive admission to a college and want to use PM-Vidyalaxmi.

Don't start by assuming that every recognised college automatically qualifies.

Check the institution on the PM-Vidyalaxmi portal first. The portal publishes an eligible-institute list using institutional information such as AISHE data.

That one check can save you from preparing a loan application around an institution that does not meet the scheme's eligibility requirements.

What Is the PM-Vidyalaxmi Income Limit?

For the 3% interest-subvention benefit, the official PM-Vidyalaxmi FAQ states that students with annual family income up to ₹8 lakh can be eligible, subject to the scheme's other conditions and the annual limit on beneficiaries. Students with annual family income up to ₹4.5 lakh may receive full interest subvention during the moratorium for eligible loans.

There are therefore two income figures that students should not mix up:

  • Up to ₹8 lakh family income: eligible students can receive 3% interest subvention during the moratorium, subject to scheme conditions.

  • Up to ₹4.5 lakh family income: eligible students can receive full interest subvention during the moratorium for qualifying loans.

These are interest-support thresholds, not simply two different scholarship amounts.

What Is the PM-Vidyalaxmi Loan Benefit?

The scheme creates a special education-loan product for eligible students.

One of its major features is that the education loan can be collateral-free and guarantor-free under the scheme's applicable conditions. The government also provides a credit guarantee covering eligible education loans up to ₹7.5 lakh at 75% credit guarantee support.

This can be particularly useful for families that may struggle to provide property or another form of collateral for an education loan.

But there is an important distinction.

Collateral-free does not mean free education.

The student still takes an education loan from a participating bank and remains responsible for repayment according to the loan terms.

What Is the PM-Vidyalaxmi Interest Subsidy?

The interest benefit is one of the most useful parts of the scheme.

For eligible students with family income up to ₹8 lakh, the scheme provides 3% interest subvention during the moratorium period on eligible education loans up to ₹10 lakh.

Students with family income up to ₹4.5 lakh can receive full interest subvention during the moratorium for eligible loans under the applicable provisions.

What does moratorium mean here?

The moratorium is the period around the student's study period and the applicable post-study period during which repayment conditions are different from the normal repayment phase.

The exact loan terms are still determined through the lending bank and applicable rules. Students should therefore check the bank's current loan terms rather than assuming that every education loan will have identical repayment conditions.

Is PM-Vidyalaxmi a Scholarship?

Not in the usual sense.

PM-Vidyalaxmi is primarily an education-loan support scheme. The government supports eligible students through loan-related benefits and interest subvention rather than simply giving every selected student a fixed annual scholarship amount.

This is one of the most common points of confusion.

If you are searching for a scheme that directly gives you a fixed amount every year without taking an education loan, PM-Vidyalaxmi is not the right way to understand this scheme.

Which Colleges Are Covered?

PM-Vidyalaxmi applies to eligible Quality Higher Educational Institutions (QHEIs) identified under the scheme.

The official portal provides an institute-search facility and publishes the eligible institution list. The list can change as institutions are added or clarified under government notices.

This is worth checking every time you apply.

For example, the Ministry issued a public notice in 2026 clarifying the eligibility of certain constituent institutions under the PM-Vidyalaxmi framework.

So don't rely on an old article that simply says a particular college is eligible. Check the current portal listing.

Are Management Quota Admissions Eligible?

No. Education loans under the PM-Vidyalaxmi Scheme are not eligible for students admitted through management quota.

This is specifically stated in the official PM-Vidyalaxmi FAQ.

Important: Getting admission to a college is not enough by itself. The admission route can also matter.

If your admission was through a management quota, don't assume that you can claim the PM-Vidyalaxmi benefit simply because the institution appears on the eligible list.

How to Apply for PM-Vidyalaxmi

The application process is online through the PM-Vidyalaxmi portal.

The basic process is:

Step 1: Register on the portal

Create your student account using your required personal information.

The portal asks for details such as your name, mobile number and email address. Your name should match the relevant educational record as required by the portal.

Step 2: Fill the education-loan application

After registration, complete the Common Education Loan Application Form.

You will need to provide information about:

  • Personal details

  • Course

  • Institution

  • Admission

  • Education expenses

  • Bank preferences

  • Other required information

Step 3: Upload documents

The official FAQ lists documents such as:

  • Class 10 marksheet

  • Class 12 or last qualifying examination marksheet

  • Proof of admission

  • Course expense schedule

  • Income proof

  • Applicant photograph

  • Parent photograph, where required

  • Co-obligant/guarantor photograph where collateral security is being provided

The portal's current requirements should be checked before submission because document requirements can change.

Step 4: Select a bank

The PM-Vidyalaxmi portal allows students to search for education-loan options and select banks according to their requirements and eligibility.

The portal states that students can select banks while applying through the unified system.

Step 5: Submit the application

Review every field before final submission.

A small mismatch in your name, admission details, course information or bank information can create unnecessary delays.

Step 6: Track the application

After submission, the application is routed to the selected bank for processing.

The portal allows students to track the status of their loan application and respond to bank queries or document requests.

What Documents Should You Keep Ready?

Before starting the application, keep your documents together.

A basic preparation checklist is:

  • Class 10 marksheet

  • Class 12 or latest qualifying examination marksheet

  • Admission letter/proof of admission

  • Course fee and expense details

  • Income certificate or other accepted income proof

  • Photograph

  • Aadhaar and other identity information as required

  • Bank-related information

  • Parent/co-obligant documents where applicable

Don't wait until the application form asks for each document. Keeping everything ready makes the process much easier.

Is Aadhaar Mandatory?

The official PM-Vidyalaxmi FAQ states that submission of Aadhaar is mandatory for availing benefits under the PM-Vidyalaxmi Scheme, including education loans, interest subvention and credit-guarantee coverage.

Make sure your identity details are consistent across the documents you submit.

If your name appears differently on your educational records and identity documents, resolve the issue or follow the portal's instructions before submitting the application.

How Is the Interest-Subvention Benefit Decided?

The scheme has a yearly limit for the number of students who can receive the 3% interest-subvention benefit.

The official FAQ states that a maximum of one lakh students can receive the 3% interest subvention in a year. If the number of fresh applicants is higher than the available number, a sequential preference system is used.

The stated preference factors include:

  1. Admission to a government higher-education institution

  2. Technical or professional courses

  3. Passing Class 12 from a government school

  4. Passing Class 10 from a government school

  5. Passing higher secondary from a rural school

  6. Girl students

This means meeting the ₹8 lakh income condition alone does not guarantee the 3% interest-subvention benefit when the number of eligible applicants exceeds the annual limit.

That is a detail students should understand before planning their finances around the subsidy.

What Happens After You Apply?

Submitting the form does not mean that the education loan has already been approved.

The application goes to the selected bank.

The bank reviews the application, documents, admission details and other applicable requirements. If the loan is sanctioned and disbursed, the bank updates the application status on the portal.

The official portal also allows students to monitor their application and respond to requests from the bank.

So keep checking the dashboard after submission.

Don't assume that no message means everything is fine.

Common Mistakes Students Should Avoid

1. Checking only the income limit

A family income below ₹8 lakh does not automatically make every student eligible for the 3% interest benefit.

Check the institution, admission route, course and other conditions too.

2. Assuming every college is eligible

The scheme uses an eligible QHEI list.

Check your institution on the current PM-Vidyalaxmi portal.

3. Ignoring the management-quota rule

Management-quota admissions are not eligible for education loans under the PM-Vidyalaxmi Scheme.

4. Treating the scheme as a cash scholarship

PM-Vidyalaxmi is mainly an education-loan support mechanism.

The loan still has to be repaid according to the applicable bank terms.

5. Uploading unclear documents

A blurry document or mismatched information can create unnecessary delays.

Upload readable documents in the format and size accepted by the portal.

6. Stopping after submitting the form

Track the application.

If the bank asks for additional information, respond through the appropriate process.

PM-Vidyalaxmi vs a Normal Education Loan

Feature

PM-Vidyalaxmi

Normal Education Loan

Online unified application

Yes

Depends on bank

Eligible QHEI requirement

Yes for PM-Vidyalaxmi benefit

Depends on bank/product

Collateral-free/guarantor-free facility

Available under scheme conditions

Depends on lender and loan amount

Government interest support

Available to eligible students

Not automatically

3% interest subvention

Eligible students with family income up to ₹8 lakh, subject to conditions

Not a standard feature

Available for eligible students with family income up to ₹4.5 lakh during applicable moratorium

Not a standard feature

Management quota

What Should You Check Before Applying?

Before submitting your application, answer these questions:

  • Is my institution currently listed as eligible?

  • Did I obtain admission through an eligible route?

  • Is my course covered?

  • What is my family's annual income?

  • Am I applying for the education loan through the PM-Vidyalaxmi portal?

  • Do my educational documents have matching personal details?

  • Do I have proof of admission?

  • Do I have the required income documents?

  • Have I provided the required Aadhaar information?

  • Have I checked the current bank requirements?

  • Will I be able to repay the education loan after the moratorium?

That last question deserves attention.

Government interest support can reduce the cost of borrowing for eligible students, but an education loan remains a financial obligation. Before borrowing, calculate the expected repayment amount and understand the bank's interest rate, repayment period and other terms.

PM-Vidyalaxmi Frequently Asked Questions

What is the PM-Vidyalaxmi Scheme?

PM-Vidyalaxmi is a Central Sector Scheme that supports eligible students pursuing higher education in India through education loans and interest-subvention benefits. Students apply through the unified PM-Vidyalaxmi portal, while the selected bank processes the education-loan application.

What is the PM-Vidyalaxmi income limit?

The family-income limit for the 3% interest-subvention benefit is ₹8 lakh per year, subject to other scheme conditions and the annual beneficiary limit. Students with family income up to ₹4.5 lakh can receive full interest subvention during the applicable moratorium for eligible loans.

How much interest subsidy is available?

Eligible students with annual family income up to ₹8 lakh can receive 3% interest subvention during the moratorium period on eligible education loans up to ₹10 lakh. The scheme also provides full interest subvention during the moratorium for eligible students with family income up to ₹4.5 lakh.

Is PM-Vidyalaxmi a scholarship?

It is primarily an education-loan support scheme, not a conventional scholarship that pays a fixed annual amount directly to every student.

Are management quota students eligible?

No. The official PM-Vidyalaxmi FAQ states that education loans under the scheme are not eligible for students admitted through management quota.

Is Aadhaar required?

Yes. The official PM-Vidyalaxmi FAQ states that Aadhaar submission is mandatory for availing benefits under the scheme, including education loans, interest subvention and credit-guarantee coverage.

Where do I apply?

Applications are made through the official PM-Vidyalaxmi portal.

Can I track my application online?

Yes. The PM-Vidyalaxmi portal provides application-status tracking and allows students to respond to bank queries or document requests.

Check the Official Portal Before Applying

Government schemes can change. Eligible institutions can also be updated through later notices.

For that reason, use the current portal when you are ready to apply rather than relying only on an old article, screenshot or social-media post.

posts.title: National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) 2026–27: Eligibility, ₹12,000 Scholarship, Exam, Application and Renewal
posts.content:
The National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) provides a scholarship of ₹12,000 a year to selected students from economically weaker families. The parental income limit is ₹3.5 lakh a year, and students must meet the prescribed Class 7 academic requirement and qualify through the State/UT selection examination. The scholarship starts from Class 9 and can continue up to Class 12.

2026–27 update: The National Scholarship Portal currently lists NMMSS as open from 1 June 2026, with the student application deadline shown as 30 September 2026. Verification dates are scheduled after the student application window. Always check the live NSP listing before submitting because dates can change.

NMMSS at a Glance

ParticularDetails
SchemeNational Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme
Scholarship amount₹12,000 per year
Monthly equivalent₹1,000 per month
Fresh scholarshipStarts from Class 9
Maximum durationUp to 4 years, Classes 9 to 12
Family income limit₹3.5 lakh per year
Income consideredParental income from all sources
Selection stageClass 8 selection examination
Academic requirementMinimum 55% or equivalent grade in Class 7
Relaxation5% relaxation for SC/ST students under the central guidelines
School eligibilityGovernment, government-aided and local body schools
Not coveredPrivate schools, Kendriya Vidyalayas and Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas
Application portalNational Scholarship Portal (NSP)
Payment methodDirect Benefit Transfer (DBT)
Exam componentsMental Ability Test (MAT) and Scholastic Aptitude Test (SAT)
2026–27 NSP opening1 June 2026
Current 2026–27 student deadline30 September 2026

The scheme guidelines provide for 1,00,000 fresh scholarships each year. Each State and Union Territory receives a prescribed quota, so qualifying for the examination does not mean that every candidate will automatically receive a scholarship.

What is the National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme?

NMMSS is a Central Sector scholarship scheme designed to help meritorious students from economically weaker families continue their education after Class 8.

The basic idea is straightforward.

A student may have the ability to continue studying but face financial pressure at the point when schooling moves into the secondary stage. NMMSS attempts to reduce that pressure by providing financial assistance from Class 9 onwards.

The Ministry of Education describes the scheme as a measure to reduce dropout after Class 8 and encourage students to continue their education through the secondary stage. One lakh fresh scholarships are awarded to selected Class 9 students each year, with renewal continuing through Classes 10, 11 and 12 when the renewal conditions are met.

This is not a scholarship that you simply claim because your Class 7 marks are high.

There are two sides to the eligibility test:

  • Means: Your family must fall within the prescribed income limit.
  • Merit: You must meet the academic requirement and qualify through the selection process conducted by your State or UT.

That combination is what gives the scheme its name: Means-cum-Merit.

What is the NMMSS scholarship amount?

The NMMSS scholarship amount is ₹12,000 per year, which works out to ₹1,000 per month when expressed as a monthly amount. The scholarship is intended for selected students from Class 9 and may continue through Class 12, subject to renewal requirements.

For a student who receives the scholarship for all four years, the total nominal assistance would be:

₹12,000 × 4 years = ₹48,000

That does not mean every selected student will automatically receive ₹48,000. Renewal is required, and the student must continue to satisfy the applicable conditions.

The amount is transferred through the government payment system rather than handed over as cash at school. NMMSS payments are made through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) system using PFMS.

How much does NMMSS give per month?

The annual scholarship of ₹12,000 is equivalent to ₹1,000 per month.

The official scheme guidelines describe the scholarship as ₹12,000 per annum at ₹1,000 per month. Students should therefore think of ₹12,000 as the annual scholarship figure when checking scheme information, even though the monthly equivalent is useful for understanding the amount.

What is the NMMSS income limit?

The NMMSS family income limit is ₹3.5 lakh per year. The official guidelines specify that parental income from all sources must not exceed ₹3,50,000 per annum at the time of selection. Students above this prescribed income ceiling do not meet the means requirement for the scholarship.

This is one of the first things a family should check.

There is little point spending time preparing for the selection process if the income condition is not satisfied.

The relevant figure is annual parental income from all sources, not simply the salary shown on one payslip.

If your family income situation has changed, use the income documentation and rules applicable to the current application cycle rather than relying on an old certificate.

Quick check

Ask:

  • Is the annual parental income within ₹3.5 lakh?
  • Do you have the required income documentation?
  • Does the document cover the period required for the application?
  • Does the information match what you enter on NSP?

A mismatch can create problems during verification even when the student otherwise meets the basic conditions.

Who can apply for NMMSS?

NMMSS is aimed at students who meet both the means and merit requirements.

For a fresh scholarship, the central guidelines require the student to have obtained at least 55% marks or an equivalent grade in Class 7 to appear in the Class 8 selection test. A 5% relaxation is provided for SC/ST students under the scheme guidelines.

The student must also be studying as a regular student in an eligible school.

The eligible school categories include:

  • Government schools
  • Government-aided schools
  • Local body schools

The scheme does not cover every type of school.

Students studying in private schools, Kendriya Vidyalayas and Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas are not eligible under the central NMMSS guidelines. Residential schools run by Central or State Government institutions that provide boarding, lodging and education are also excluded under the guidelines.

NMMSS eligibility checklist

Before looking at the examination details, check these points:

  1. You are studying in an eligible school.
  2. You have the required Class 7 marks or equivalent grade.
  3. Your parental income is within ₹3.5 lakh per year.
  4. You are appearing for the selection examination conducted by your State/UT.
  5. You qualify through the State/UT selection process.
  6. You meet the renewal requirements in later classes if you continue receiving the scholarship.

This simple checklist can save a lot of confusion.

How are NMMSS students selected?

NMMSS selection is conducted through an examination organized by the respective State Government or Union Territory Administration.

The central guidelines specify two parts of the selection test:

  • Mental Ability Test (MAT)
  • Scholastic Aptitude Test (SAT)

The examination is held at the Class 8 stage.

This means a student cannot simply apply on NSP and wait for the scholarship to be approved. The selection examination is a central part of the process.

The exact examination arrangements, dates, application instructions and operational details can vary by State/UT. Students should therefore check their State's official education department or scholarship authority notices alongside the central scheme information.

What is the NMMSS Mental Ability Test (MAT)?

The Mental Ability Test (MAT) checks reasoning and thinking abilities rather than simply asking students to reproduce textbook answers.

The central guidelines describe MAT as a test of verbal and non-verbal abilities, including areas such as:

  • Analogy
  • Classification
  • Numerical series
  • Pattern perception
  • Hidden figures
  • Reasoning
  • Critical thinking

The guidelines specify 90 multiple-choice questions for the MAT component.

This is useful to know before preparing.

A student who only studies school chapters and ignores reasoning practice may find the selection test quite different from an ordinary school examination.

How should students prepare for MAT?

A practical preparation routine can include:

  • Number and letter series
  • Analogies
  • Classification questions
  • Figure-based reasoning
  • Pattern recognition
  • Coding and decoding
  • Logical relationships
  • Mental calculation
  • Previous State-level question papers where available

The goal is not to memorize hundreds of answers.

Practice helps you recognize the type of problem quickly.

What is the NMMSS Scholastic Aptitude Test (SAT)?

The Scholastic Aptitude Test (SAT) checks academic understanding.

The exact State/UT examination structure should be verified from the relevant State authority because implementation details can vary. The central NMMSS framework includes SAT as one of the two selection-test components.

Students should prepare using the prescribed school-level syllabus and the examination instructions issued by their State or UT.

A common mistake is to treat MAT and SAT as completely separate exams and spend all preparation time on one of them.

Don't.

Your selection depends on the overall prescribed process.

When does NMMSS start paying the scholarship?

A fresh NMMSS scholarship is awarded to selected students entering Class 9.

The scholarship can continue through Classes 10, 11 and 12, subject to the renewal conditions. The central guidelines describe the scholarship as being provided for a maximum period of four years.

So the normal progression looks like this:

ClassNMMSS status
Class 7Academic qualification stage
Class 8Selection examination
Class 9Fresh scholarship begins
Class 10Renewal
Class 11Renewal
Class 12Renewal

This is why the Class 8 examination matters so much. Missing the selection stage can mean missing the opportunity to enter the scheme as a fresh beneficiary.

How to apply for NMMSS through NSP

For the current academic year, NMMSS is available through the National Scholarship Portal.

The NSP currently lists the 2026–27 NMMSS student application window as opening on 1 June 2026 and closing on 30 September 2026. The portal also lists subsequent defective-application and verification stages.

Step 1: Complete One Time Registration

NSP requires an One Time Registration (OTR) number for scholarship applications from academic year 2024–25 onward.

Keep your OTR details safe.

Do not share your OTP, password or other sensitive login information with another person.

Step 2: Log in to NSP

Use the official National Scholarship Portal and access the student application section.

Step 3: Select NMMSS

Find the National Means Cum Merit Scholarship scheme listed under the Department of School Education & Literacy.

The current NSP listing identifies it as a Merit Based Scheme.

Step 4: Complete the application

Enter the requested information carefully.

Check:

  • Student name
  • Date of birth
  • School details
  • Class
  • Bank information
  • Aadhaar-related information where requested
  • Income information
  • Academic details

Don't rush this section.

A small spelling difference between documents can create a verification problem later.

Step 5: Submit the application

Review everything before final submission.

Save or download the acknowledgement/application details after submission.

Step 6: Track verification

Submission is not the same thing as final approval.

The application goes through the prescribed verification process. NSP provides facilities for tracking scholarship applications and for grievance registration.

What happens if the NMMSS application is defective?

A defective application does not necessarily mean the student has permanently lost the scholarship.

If the portal or verifier marks an application as defective, read the reason shown in the application status carefully.

The problem could relate to information or documentation that needs correction.

The correct response is to:

  1. Log in to NSP.
  2. Read the defect reason.
  3. Identify the incorrect or missing information.
  4. Make the permitted correction.
  5. Resubmit within the specified correction period.

Do not create a second application simply because you are worried about the first one.

Follow the instructions shown by NSP.

For 2026–27, the current NSP listing shows defective-application verification continuing after the student application deadline.

How is the NMMSS scholarship paid?

NMMSS scholarship payments are made through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).

The Ministry has stated that NMMSS scholarships are transferred directly to beneficiaries' bank accounts through the Public Financial Management System (PFMS).

This makes bank-account details a practical part of the application process.

Before submitting your application, check that the bank information you provide is correct and that the account can receive the applicable government payment.

The NSP has also highlighted Aadhaar seeding and DBT-related processes in its current student notices.

NMMSS renewal: What happens after Class 9?

Getting selected in Class 8 is only the beginning.

NMMSS can continue from Class 9 through Class 12, but the scholarship is not simply a one-time payment covering all four years.

Students have to satisfy the applicable renewal requirements.

The scheme is designed around continued education, so maintaining academic progress and complying with the renewal process matters.

Don't assume that because you received ₹12,000 in one year, the next year's payment will arrive automatically.

Check NSP renewal instructions when the new application cycle opens.

Can private school students get NMMSS?

No.

The central NMMSS guidelines specifically exclude students studying in private schools. The scheme is intended for regular students in government, government-aided and local body schools.

This is one of the easiest eligibility checks to make.

If your school is private, the NMMSS central scheme is not the right scholarship to apply for, even if your marks and family income satisfy the other conditions.

Can Kendriya Vidyalaya students apply for NMMSS?

No.

Students studying in Kendriya Vidyalayas are not eligible under the NMMSS guidelines.

The same exclusion applies to Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas.

This is worth checking before spending time preparing documents or searching for the application link.

Is NMMSS only for students with very high marks?

Not exactly.

NMMSS is a merit-cum-means scheme. A student must satisfy the financial condition and the prescribed academic requirement, then qualify through the State/UT selection process.

The Class 7 requirement is a minimum of 55% or equivalent grade, with the specified 5% relaxation for SC/ST students.

But clearing the Class 7 marks requirement does not itself guarantee selection.

The examination matters.

Is NMMSS a first-come, first-served scholarship?

No.

NMMSS is a merit-based selection scheme.

Students must go through the prescribed State/UT examination process. The central guidelines provide a fixed allocation of scholarships across States/UTs, and selection takes place within that framework.

So submitting an application early does not replace the merit and selection requirements.

How many NMMSS scholarships are available?

The scheme provides for 1,00,000 fresh scholarships each year.

These scholarships are distributed among States and Union Territories according to the prescribed allocation framework.

The government's 2026–27 output framework also sets a target of 1,00,000 Class 9 beneficiaries, alongside targets for continuing beneficiaries in Classes 10, 11 and 12.

This is an important distinction:

1,00,000 is the national fresh-scholarship target. It does not mean that every State has unlimited scholarships.

Common mistakes students should avoid

NMMSS applications are easier when you know where problems usually arise.

Applying without checking the school category

A student can have good marks and low family income and still be ineligible because the school does not fall under the permitted categories.

Check this first.

Treating ₹3.5 lakh as a monthly figure

It is an annual family income limit.

Do not confuse the annual ceiling with monthly income.

Assuming 55% means automatic selection

It doesn't.

The 55% figure is the academic requirement to appear in the selection test under the central guidelines. You still have to go through the examination and selection process.

Ignoring MAT

MAT is not just another school subject.

It tests reasoning and mental ability. Give it dedicated practice time.

Waiting until the final day

Portal traffic, document problems, school verification and technical issues can become stressful when you leave everything until the deadline.

Apply early enough to correct a problem if one appears.

Ignoring renewal

A scholarship that continues through Class 12 still requires attention in later years.

Keep checking NSP notifications rather than assuming the payment will repeat automatically.

NMMSS 2026–27 application date

For the current 2026–27 academic year, the National Scholarship Portal lists:

ActivityCurrent NSP date
NMMSS student application opens1 June 2026
Student application closes30 September 2026
Defective application verification closes15 October 2026
Institute verification closes15 October 2026
DNO/SNO/MNO verification closes31 October 2026

These dates come from the current NSP scheme listing and should be treated as the live portal schedule for 2026–27.

Dates can be revised by the authorities, so check NSP again before relying on a deadline.

What documents may be required?

The exact document requirements can depend on the current application workflow and State/UT instructions.

Students should be prepared to provide information relating to:

  • Class 7 academic record
  • School details
  • Family income
  • Bank account
  • Identity/Aadhaar-related information where required
  • Category information where applicable
  • OTR details
  • Other information requested by NSP

Do not upload an old document simply because it was accepted in a previous scholarship application.

Use the documents and format requested for the current application.

NMMSS and the National Scholarship Portal

NSP is the central online platform used for NMMSS applications.

The current NSP portal states that the 2026–27 academic year portal opened from 1 June 2026 and that an OTR number is required for scholarship applications.

The portal also provides public facilities for finding registered institutes, scheme-wise nodal officers, grievance registration and helpdesk services.

That matters when something goes wrong.

You do not have to rely entirely on a school WhatsApp group or an old scholarship article to find out what to do next. The portal has official support and grievance facilities.

NMMSS is more than a ₹12,000 scholarship

₹12,000 a year may not cover every education expense.

That isn't really the point.

For a family managing school expenses carefully, ₹12,000 can still make a practical difference. More importantly, the scheme is designed to encourage students who might otherwise leave education after Class 8 to remain in school through the secondary stage.

The government's 2026–27 framework explicitly connects the scheme with continuing secondary education for students from economically weaker sections and sets beneficiary targets through Class 12.

For students and parents, the useful takeaway is simple:

Check the income limit. Check the school category. Check the Class 7 marks requirement. Prepare for MAT and SAT. Then follow the State/UT selection process and complete the NSP application and renewal requirements.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the NMMSS scholarship amount?

NMMSS provides ₹12,000 per year, equivalent to ₹1,000 per month. A selected student can receive the scholarship from Class 9 and continue through Class 12, subject to the applicable renewal conditions. The central guidelines specify a maximum duration of four years.

What is the NMMSS income limit?

The parental income limit for NMMSS is ₹3.5 lakh per year from all sources. This is a key means-based eligibility condition. Families above the prescribed annual income ceiling do not meet the income requirement for the scholarship.

What percentage is required for NMMSS?

Students generally need at least 55% marks or an equivalent grade in Class 7 to appear in the selection test. The central guidelines provide a 5% relaxation for SC/ST students. Clearing this academic requirement does not itself guarantee selection.

Which class is NMMSS for?

The selection examination is conducted at the Class 8 stage, while the scholarship is awarded to selected students entering Class 9. It can continue through Classes 10, 11 and 12 when renewal requirements are satisfied.

Can a private school student apply for NMMSS?

No. The central guidelines cover regular students studying in government, government-aided and local body schools. Students in private schools are not eligible under the NMMSS scheme.

Can Kendriya Vidyalaya students receive NMMSS?

No. The central NMMSS guidelines specifically state that students studying in Kendriya Vidyalayas and Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas are not entitled to the scholarship.

What is the NMMSS exam pattern?

The selection test includes Mental Ability Test (MAT) and Scholastic Aptitude Test (SAT). The central guidelines specify MAT as a test of verbal and non-verbal abilities, including reasoning and critical-thinking areas. State/UT authorities conduct the selection examination.

Is NMMSS available on NSP?

Yes. NMMSS is listed on the National Scholarship Portal under the Department of School Education & Literacy. The current NSP listing identifies it as a merit-based scheme.

What is the NMMSS 2026–27 last date?

The current NSP listing shows 30 September 2026 as the student application deadline for NMMSS for academic year 2026–27. Because scholarship schedules can be revised, check the live NSP listing before submitting.

How is NMMSS money paid?

The scholarship is paid through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). Government information states that NMMSS scholarships are transferred directly to selected students' bank accounts through PFMS.

Final checklist for students and parents

Before treating your NMMSS application as complete, run through this list:

  • Family income is within ₹3.5 lakh annually.

  • Student has the required Class 7 academic performance.

  • School falls under an eligible category.

  • Student is preparing for the State/UT selection examination.

  • MAT preparation is included.

  • SAT preparation is included.

  • OTR has been completed on NSP.

  • Personal and academic details have been checked.

  • Bank information is correct.

  • Application has been finally submitted.

  • Application status is being monitored.

  • Defects, if any, are corrected within the permitted period.

  • Renewal requirements are checked in subsequent years.

The safest approach is to use this article as a practical guide, then confirm the current application status, deadline and instructions on the official NSP and Ministry of Education websites before taking action.

posts.title: PM-USP Special Scholarship Scheme for Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh: Eligibility, Scholarship Amount, Fees, Maintenance Allowance and How to Apply
posts.content:
The PM-USP Special Scholarship Scheme for Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh offers up to 5,000 fresh scholarships each year to eligible students from the Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. The family income limit is ₹8 lakh per year. Students must meet the domicile, Class 12, admission and other scheme conditions before the scholarship can be awarded.

The scheme is meant to help eligible students pursue undergraduate education outside Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. It covers different streams, including general degree courses, professional courses and medical courses.

Current-cycle notice: NSP currently lists the PM-USP Special Scholarship Scheme for Jammu Kashmir and Ladakh for Academic Year 2026–27, with renewal applications shown as open from 1 June 2026 to 31 October 2026. Verification dates are also listed on NSP. Always check the live AICTE and NSP notices before acting because application windows and instructions can change.

PM-USP Special Scholarship Scheme at a Glance

ParticularDetails
SchemePM-USP Special Scholarship Scheme for Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh
Target studentsEligible students from J&K and Ladakh
Fresh scholarships5,000 per year
Family income limitUp to ₹8 lakh per year
General degree scholarships2,070
Professional course scholarships2,830
Medical scholarships100
General degree academic fee ceilingUp to ₹30,000 per year
Professional course academic fee ceilingUp to ₹1.25 lakh per year
Medical course academic fee ceilingUp to ₹3 lakh per year
Maintenance allowance₹1 lakh per beneficiary, subject to scheme rules
Application systemAICTE portal / prescribed admission process
NSPUsed for the scholarship record and renewal process for the applicable cycle
Major exclusionManagement-quota admission
Other major exclusionsDiploma, postgraduate study, open university courses and certain other categories

The Ministry of Education records the annual allocation as 5,000 fresh scholarships: 2,070 for general degree courses, 2,830 for professional courses and 100 for medical courses.

What is the PM-USP Special Scholarship Scheme for J&K and Ladakh?

The PM-USP Special Scholarship Scheme is a Central Government scholarship programme for eligible students from Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh who want to pursue higher education outside these Union Territories.

The basic idea is straightforward. A student who meets the scheme conditions can receive financial assistance towards academic fees and maintenance while studying at an eligible institution.

The Ministry of Education describes the scheme as a way to encourage students from J&K and Ladakh to study in educational institutions outside the UTs and gain exposure to educational, cultural and social environments in other parts of India.

This is not simply a scholarship that pays money after you take admission anywhere.

The admission route matters.

The institution matters.

The course matters.

Your family income matters.

And the way you register and complete the prescribed counselling or admission process matters.

That is where many students make mistakes.

Who can apply for the PMSSS J&K and Ladakh scholarship?

Students must satisfy the applicable eligibility requirements rather than relying on marks or income alone.

The official scheme guidelines identify these major conditions:

  • You must be a domicile of the Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir or Ladakh.
  • You must have passed Class 12 from JKBOSE or a CBSE-affiliated school located in J&K or Ladakh, subject to the applicable scheme rules.
  • Your annual family income must not exceed ₹8 lakh.
  • Lateral-entry applicants must meet the prescribed diploma requirements.
  • You must complete the required online registration through the prescribed AICTE system.
  • You must complete document verification through the designated process within the prescribed period.
  • Admission must follow the scheme's prescribed route and participating-institution conditions.

What is the PMSSS income limit?

The family income limit for PMSSS is ₹8 lakh per year. Students from eligible J&K and Ladakh families must satisfy this income condition along with the other scheme requirements. A student who has strong academic performance but whose family income exceeds the prescribed ceiling does not qualify merely because of high marks.

Keep the income certificate information consistent with your application. A mismatch between documents and the information submitted online can create problems during verification.

How many students get the scholarship every year?

The scheme provides 5,000 fresh scholarships every year.

The broad allocation is:

Course categoryFresh scholarships
General Degree Courses2,070
Professional Courses2,830
Medical Courses100
Total5,000

These numbers are part of the scheme's published allocation. They should not be interpreted as a promise that every applicant who meets a basic eligibility condition will automatically receive a scholarship. Admission, merit, available seats, counselling and the applicable scheme rules still matter.

What is the PMSSS scholarship amount?

The scholarship has two major components: academic fee support and a maintenance allowance.

The published AICTE material gives the following academic-fee ceilings:

Course typeAcademic fee support
General DegreeUp to ₹30,000
Professional DegreeUp to ₹1.25 lakh
Medical / BDS or equivalent medical streamsUp to ₹3 lakh

The scheme material also provides a ₹1 lakh maintenance allowance for the beneficiary, with the official guidelines specifying the payment structure.

What is the PMSSS maintenance allowance?

The PMSSS maintenance allowance is ₹1 lakh per beneficiary under the published scheme guidelines. The guidelines state that from the second year onward, the fixed maintenance allowance is paid in 10 monthly instalments of ₹10,000 each. Students should follow the payment and renewal instructions applicable to their academic year.

This money is intended to help with the everyday cost of studying away from home.

That can include expenses such as accommodation, food, travel, books and other educational needs. The scholarship should not be treated as a replacement for every personal expense a student may have.

What does the scholarship cover?

The financial assistance is designed around two broad needs.

1. Academic fees

The scheme provides financial support up to the prescribed ceiling for the student's course category.

The ceiling differs considerably between a general degree and a professional or medical programme.

For example, the published figures provide:

  • Up to ₹30,000 for general degree courses
  • Up to ₹1.25 lakh for professional degree courses
  • Up to ₹3 lakh for medical/BDS or equivalent medical streams

Do not assume that the government will automatically pay whatever fee a private college charges.

The published amount is a ceiling under the scheme.

2. Maintenance support

Students also receive maintenance assistance subject to the applicable rules.

The official guidelines specify a fixed maintenance allowance of ₹1 lakh and state that from the second year onward it is paid in 10 monthly instalments of ₹10,000 each.

A simple example of the fee ceiling

Suppose you join an eligible professional course and the academic fee is ₹1.10 lakh.

The fee falls within the published ₹1.25 lakh professional-course ceiling.

Now consider a different college charging ₹1.80 lakh.

You should not assume that the complete ₹1.80 lakh will automatically be covered simply because you are a PMSSS beneficiary. The scheme's prescribed ceiling and applicable institutional rules still apply.

This distinction matters when comparing colleges.

Look at the actual fee structure before finalising your admission.

Important: Management-quota admission can make you ineligible

The official guidelines specifically list candidates taking admission through Management Quota among the categories not eligible under the scheme.

Do not pay a college agent or private intermediary first and assume the scholarship will be added later.

The admission route needs to comply with the scheme.

The published AICTE material also lists admission through agents or NGOs as an exclusion and requires students to use the prescribed online registration and admission process.

If somebody tells you that you can bypass the official process by paying an additional amount to secure a seat, verify that claim with AICTE before paying.

Which courses are covered?

The scheme has separate allocations for:

  • General degree courses
  • Professional degree courses
  • Medical courses

Professional courses listed in AICTE material include areas such as:

  • Engineering
  • Nursing
  • Hotel Management and Catering Technology
  • Architecture
  • Pharmacy
  • B.Sc. Nursing

The exact participating courses and institutions should be checked against the current AICTE portal and applicable admission information rather than relying on an old college list.

Are diploma courses covered?

No.

Diploma courses are listed among the exclusions in the published scheme guidelines.

There is a separate provision for eligible lateral entry candidates who have completed a qualifying diploma in engineering from a recognised polytechnic in J&K or Ladakh. The guidelines state that such admission is subject to the available seats and prescribed conditions, including the relevant engineering stream.

So there is an important difference:

A normal diploma course is not covered as a scholarship course, but a qualifying engineering diploma can be relevant for lateral entry under the specific scheme provision.

Can postgraduate students apply?

No.

The published exclusions state that candidates pursuing postgraduate-level studies are not eligible under the scheme.

The scheme is primarily focused on undergraduate-level higher education and the categories specifically covered by its guidelines.

Can students studying through an open university apply?

No.

The official guidelines list candidates pursuing courses through Open Universities among the categories that are not eligible.

This is one reason you should check the mode of study before applying.

A course being offered by a recognised institution does not automatically mean that it qualifies for PMSSS.

Can you take another scholarship along with PMSSS?

The published scheme guidelines exclude students who are availing benefits from another scholarship scheme operated by a Central Government, State Government, UT Government or an autonomous body under them.

Do not make assumptions here.

If you already receive another scholarship, fee reimbursement or government educational benefit, check the applicable rules before accepting both benefits.

Important: Check the bank account before expecting payment

Scholarship payments are processed through government payment systems, so your banking details need to be correct.

NSP also provides information about Aadhaar seeding and DBT-related services, including the Bharat Aadhaar Seeding Enabler (BASE).

Do not enter somebody else's bank account simply because it is convenient.

Before expecting a scholarship payment, check:

  • Your name in the bank account
  • Account number
  • IFSC
  • Aadhaar linkage/seeding status where required
  • Whether the account is active
  • Whether the details entered in the application match your documents

A small banking mismatch can turn into a payment problem later.

How to apply for PMSSS

The application process has historically involved the prescribed AICTE online system, document verification and counselling/admission procedures.

The exact dates and steps can change for a new academic cycle, so students should use the current AICTE instructions rather than following an old YouTube video or an outdated blog post.

A typical process involves:

Step 1: Check eligibility

Before registering, confirm:

  • J&K/Ladakh domicile
  • Class 12 qualification
  • Family income within ₹8 lakh
  • Eligible course
  • Eligible admission route
  • Other applicable conditions

Step 2: Register through the prescribed AICTE portal

The official guidelines require eligible candidates to apply online through the AICTE web portal.

Step 3: Complete document verification

The guidelines require document verification through designated Facilitation Centres in J&K and Ladakh within the prescribed time frame.

Do not leave this until the last day.

If a document has a problem, you need enough time to resolve it.

Step 4: Participate in the prescribed counselling process

Eligible students are placed through the applicable merit and counselling process.

The guidelines state that the merit list for Higher Secondary Certificate and lateral-entry students is displayed through the student portal for online counselling and final allotment, subject to choice filling and scholarship availability.

Step 5: Take admission at the allotted or eligible institution

This step is critical.

Do not independently switch to a college or course without checking whether the new admission remains eligible under PMSSS.

The official material specifically restricts scholarship eligibility to prescribed participating institutions and admission routes.

What happens if you join a college outside the approved process?

This can put the scholarship at risk.

The published guidelines list admission to colleges other than the prescribed institutions on the AICTE portal among the exclusions. They also exclude management-quota admissions and admissions through agents or NGOs.

That is why students should not treat PMSSS as a reimbursement scheme where they can first choose any college and ask the government to pay later.

The admission itself must fit the scheme.

PMSSS renewal for existing students

Getting the scholarship once does not mean you can ignore the portal in later academic years.

Existing beneficiaries need to follow the applicable renewal process and academic requirements.

For 2026–27, NSP lists the PM-USP Special Scholarship Scheme for Jammu Kashmir and Ladakh under renewal applications from 1 June 2026 to 31 October 2026. NSP also lists defective-application verification through 15 November 2026, institute verification through 15 November 2026, and DNO/SNO/MNO verification through 30 November 2026.

These dates are specifically for the 2026–27 NSP renewal listing. Always check the live portal before relying on them.

PMSSS 2026–27 important dates

Activity2026–27 date shown on NSP
NSP renewal opens1 June 2026
Student application deadline31 October 2026
Defective application verification15 November 2026
Institute verification15 November 2026
DNO/SNO/MNO verification30 November 2026

NSP identifies these dates for the renewal listing of the PM-USP Special Scholarship Scheme for Jammu Kashmir and Ladakh.

Fresh applicants should not assume that the NSP renewal dates are the same as the AICTE fresh-admission schedule. Fresh admission and renewal are different parts of the process, so check the current AICTE notification for the applicable fresh-admission cycle.

What documents should students keep ready?

The exact document list can vary according to the application and verification process, but students should be prepared to provide documents supporting the information entered in the application.

Commonly relevant documents include:

  • Domicile certificate
  • Class 10 certificate
  • Class 12 marksheet/certificate
  • Income certificate
  • Aadhaar details
  • Bank account information
  • Passport-size photograph
  • Relevant category or other certificates, where applicable
  • Documents required for lateral entry, where applicable

Do not upload an old or incorrect income certificate simply because it is already available at home.

Check the current instructions first.

What can cause problems with a PMSSS application?

A student can satisfy the basic academic conditions and still run into trouble because of an administrative mistake.

Watch these areas closely:

Wrong income information

The ₹8 lakh ceiling is a core eligibility condition.

Incorrect admission route

Management-quota admission is specifically excluded.

Choosing the wrong institution

The guidelines restrict scholarship eligibility to prescribed participating institutions.

Applying through an agent

The official material lists admission through agents or NGOs as an exclusion.

Missing document verification

Online registration alone is not enough. The guidelines require the prescribed verification process.

Assuming every course is covered

Diploma and postgraduate programmes are excluded, while professional and medical courses have their own categories and conditions.

A practical checklist before you apply

Before submitting anything, stop for five minutes and check the basics.

Eligibility

  • I have the required J&K/Ladakh domicile.

  • I passed the qualifying examination from the required location.

  • My family income is within ₹8 lakh.

  • My course falls under an eligible category.

  • I am not applying for an excluded programme.

Admission

  • I followed the prescribed AICTE process.

  • My institution is within the eligible participating pool.

  • My admission is not through management quota.

  • I did not use an agent or NGO to obtain the scholarship seat.

Documents

  • My name is consistent across important documents.

  • My income information is correct.

  • My bank details are correct.

  • My required verification has been completed.

Renewal

  • I checked the current NSP renewal dates.

  • I have completed the required renewal application.

  • I have checked my application status after submission.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the PMSSS income limit?

The PMSSS family income limit is ₹8 lakh per year. The income condition applies alongside the domicile, academic, admission and other eligibility requirements. A student cannot qualify solely because the family income is below ₹8 lakh; every applicable condition must be satisfied.

How many PMSSS scholarships are available each year?

The scheme provides 5,000 fresh scholarships every year. The published allocation includes 2,070 scholarships for general degree courses, 2,830 for professional courses and 100 for medical courses.

What is the PMSSS maintenance allowance?

The published scheme guidelines provide a ₹1 lakh maintenance allowance per beneficiary. From the second year onward, the guidelines specify payment in 10 monthly instalments of ₹10,000 each. Students should follow the payment rules applicable to their academic year.

What is the PMSSS scholarship amount for general degree courses?

For general degree courses, the published academic-fee ceiling is up to ₹30,000. The scheme also provides maintenance assistance subject to its applicable rules. The academic-fee ceiling is not the same thing as a guarantee that every student's actual college fee will be paid in full.

What is the PMSSS scholarship amount for professional courses?

For eligible professional degree courses, the published academic-fee ceiling is up to ₹1.25 lakh. The professional-course allocation contains 2,830 fresh scholarships in the published scheme material.

What is the PMSSS medical scholarship amount?

For eligible medical, BDS or equivalent medical streams, the published academic-fee ceiling is up to ₹3 lakh. The medical category has an allocation of 100 fresh scholarships in the published scheme material.

Can I get PMSSS through management quota?

No. Management-quota admission is listed as an exclusion under the scheme. Students should follow the prescribed AICTE registration, counselling and admission process instead of assuming that a management-quota seat can later be converted into a scholarship-supported admission.

Can diploma students get PMSSS?

A normal diploma programme is excluded. However, the scheme has a specific lateral-entry provision for eligible engineering diploma holders from recognised polytechnic institutions in J&K and Ladakh, subject to the applicable conditions and available seats.

Can postgraduate students receive PMSSS?

No. The published guidelines list candidates pursuing postgraduate-level studies among the excluded categories.

Can students studying through an open university apply?

No. Courses through Open Universities are specifically listed among the exclusions in the published guidelines.

Is the ₹8 lakh income limit enough to guarantee the scholarship?

No. Income is only one eligibility condition. Domicile, qualifying examination, course, admission route, participating institution, registration, verification and other applicable conditions must also be satisfied.

Where should I check PMSSS 2026–27 updates?

Use the official National Scholarship Portal for the current scholarship and renewal information and the official AICTE PMSSS system/notices for the admission process. The NSP currently lists the PM-USP Special Scholarship Scheme for Jammu Kashmir and Ladakh for 2026–27 renewal activity.

Final checklist for students

If you remember only a few things from this guide, remember these:

5,000 fresh scholarships are available each year.

The family income ceiling is ₹8 lakh per year.

General degree, professional and medical courses have different academic-fee ceilings.

Management-quota admission is excluded.

Diploma and postgraduate programmes are excluded, subject to the specific lateral-entry provision for eligible engineering diploma holders.

The prescribed AICTE registration and verification process matters.

Do not rely on an agent promising that a private admission will qualify for PMSSS.

Check the current AICTE and NSP notices before applying or renewing.

For 2026–27, NSP currently shows the renewal application window through 31 October 2026, with subsequent verification stages extending into November.

The safest approach is simple: check your eligibility first, verify the institution and course before paying fees, complete the official registration process, keep your documents consistent, and monitor your application after submission.
